features.method: Convex hull of the 78 standard string positions of geometry:icecube-strings-1-78 (13 corner vertices, each straight edge subdivided into pieces of 10 m or less in the grid plane so that the validator's longitude-latitude area formula, which is only exact for short edges near the pole, measures the true area). It is an outline computed here to show the footprint of the 1 km3 volume, not a published boundary of the instrumented ice. Frame and anchor: the IceCube coordinate system has its y-axis along the Prime Meridian (Grid North, towards Greenwich) and its x-axis 90 degrees clockwise from it (Grid East) (IceCube instrumentation paper, arXiv v3, section 5.3), and its origin is at elevation 883.9 m. The IceCube Collaboration software repository i3astropy gives the nominal location of the centre of the detector as lat -89.9944, lon -62.6081, height 883.9 m, which is taken as the frame origin. Conversion: the origin is placed at that point in a South Pole azimuthal-equidistant plane (distance from the pole = colatitude x 6 371 008.8 m, grid north = 0 deg meridian, grid east = 90 deg E; this is the same plane the browser draws), each string is the origin plus its (x, y) offset, and the inverse projection gives lat/lon. The origin is 622.7 m from the pole on the 62.6 deg W meridian. Accuracy: the layout of the strings relative to each other is surveyed to about 1 m, and the pattern keeps its true size and orientation (grid north). The absolute position of the whole pattern is only good to about 500 m: the anchor is a nominal value of no stated epoch, the array moves with the ice about 10 m a year relative to geographic coordinates, and the lat/lon of IceCube on Wikipedia and in OpenStreetMap (89.99 S, 63.4531 W) lies 489 m from the anchor used.

features.method: Plan positions of the 78 standard in-ice strings. Each string position is the mean horizontal (x, y) of its 60 DOMs in the IC86 geometry file published in the IceCube repository icecube/toise (strings are vertical; string 21 varies by 0.33 m, every other string is identical in all 60 DOMs). Frame and anchor: the IceCube coordinate system has its y-axis along the Prime Meridian (Grid North, towards Greenwich) and its x-axis 90 degrees clockwise from it (Grid East) (IceCube instrumentation paper, arXiv v3, section 5.3), and its origin is at elevation 883.9 m. Conversion: the origin is placed at that point in a South Pole azimuthal-equidistant plane (distance from the pole = colatitude x 6 371 008.8 m, grid north = 0 deg meridian, grid east = 90 deg E; this is the same plane the browser draws), each string is the origin plus its (x, y) offset, and the inverse projection gives lat/lon. The origin is 622.7 m from the pole on the 62.6 deg W meridian. Each string is drawn as a 2 m x 2 m square aligned to grid north, a position marker only: the borehole is far smaller, so the size is symbolic and the 1 m half-width is not a claim about the hole. Accuracy: the layout of the strings relative to each other is surveyed to about 1 m, and the pattern keeps its true size and orientation (grid north). The absolute position of the whole pattern is only good to about 500 m: the anchor is a nominal value of no stated epoch, the array moves with the ice about 10 m a year relative to geographic coordinates, and the lat/lon of IceCube on Wikipedia and in OpenStreetMap (89.99 S, 63.4531 W) lies 489 m from the anchor used. Check done in the worklog: median nearest-neighbour spacing of strings 1-78 is 124.3 m against the official triangular grid of 125 m horizontal spacing.

features.method: Single OpenStreetMap node (place=village, name='Amundsen–Scott South Pole Station'), Overpass extract with out geom; using the near-pole bbox form (-90,-180,-89.98,180) as instructed, mirrors overpass-api.de then lz4.overpass-api.de. No OSM building footprint for the station or a separate IceCube Laboratory (ICL) feature was found in this query (a name-pattern search for 'Amundsen|South Pole Station' on building ways, and for 'IceCube Laboratory|ICL' on any way, returned zero elements; only this one place node matched). Used as a visible reference marker for site:south-pole-icecube's approximate location, not a claim about the true surveyed position of the array, the ICL building, or any structure; accuracy_m is set generously (300 m) because a single untagged-building 'place' node is not a survey. The node sits about 223 m from the geometric South Pole (90 - 89.998 degrees of latitude), plausible for the station's real offset from the pole marker.

summary.plain: The U.S. research station at the geographic South Pole and the IceCube neutrino telescope beside it. The map shows the 86 in-ice strings (including the dense DeepCore centre) and the 162 IceTop surface tanks at their true spacing, with grid north up; the whole pattern could be shifted by up to about half a kilometre because the ice moves and the published anchor is nominal. ARA, AMANDA, the IceCube Upgrade and IceCube-Gen2 are not drawn.

unlocated.backlog: Find a table of as-built ARA station coordinates in the South Pole grid or IceCube frame (a station-deployment paper appendix or the collaboration's geometry files); with the frame orientation now sourced, grid offsets convert with the anchor used for IceCube on this map.
unlocated.reason: ARA's five stations (A1-A5) sit about 2 km from the IceCube array, but no source fetched gives their individual coordinates, spacing or bearings. The ARA overview paper (arXiv:2411.01761) states only the ~2 km distance from IceCube, no map or per-station layout. The ARA design paper (arXiv:1105.2854) describes the baseline 37-station, 2 km hexagonal-grid concept (not the five as-built stations) and puts the 2011 testbed 'approximately 1.8 km grid East of the IceCube detector'. The grid orientation is now sourced (IceCube instrumentation paper v3, section 5.3), but an offset of a testbed is not an as-built station position and a web search on 2026-10-25 found no table of A1-A5 coordinates.

unlocated.backlog: Find an AMANDA-II string coordinate table (detector paper or the AMANDA data release README) in the AMANDA/IceCube grid; the frame is now anchored, so a table converts directly.
unlocated.reason: AMANDA's 19 strings were 'spread out in a rough circle with a diameter of 200 meters' near the IceCube array's centre (IceCube timeline, already cited on experiment:amanda), but no fetched source gives AMANDA string coordinates in the IceCube grid or an offset from the IceCube frame origin; a web search on 2026-10-25 found no coordinate table.

unlocated.backlog: Revisit once IceCube-Gen2 publishes sited string coordinates; the IceCube frame these would be given in is now anchored on this map.
unlocated.reason: IceCube-Gen2 is a proposed, not-yet-built expansion 'surrounding the existing IceCube array' (its own facility_roles note, already cited) with no published string coordinates; even its optical array's planned footprint is described only in aggregate specs (120 holes, ~500 km2 radio array), not as a sited polygon, and it inherits the same unresolved georeferencing gap as the array it surrounds.

unlocated.backlog: The as-built string coordinates in the IceCube frame: a table or geometry file for the IC93 configuration (the Upgrade GCD), or an Upgrade deployment paper listing the string numbers drilled and their horizontal positions. Strings 36, 79 and 80 of the existing array lie inside the Upgrade footprint (arXiv:2308.07276) and are already drawn from the IC86 geometry, so any set of distances to them converts directly with the anchor used on this map.
unlocated.reason: Only the DESIGN layout is published, and the as-built layout differs from it. The design has seven strings numbered 87 to 93 with horizontal spacings of 21 m to 43 m, drawn with all inter-string distances in Fig. 2 of the Upgrade camera paper (arXiv:2308.07276, a figure, not text), whereas the 2026 status paper (arXiv:2609.24387) says five strings were added in 2025/26 and shows the final layout only in a schematic (Fig. 1, no axes or coordinates); the collaboration news items count five or six strings deployed. Drawing the seven design positions would put two or more strings on the map that were never built, and no source says which of the seven the five deployed strings are.
